doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Cannonball and the Batiste soprano piece in New Orleans
summary: Cannonball played Batiste's written soprano part with Jordan covering, then promised to play some of Jordan's crazy stuff.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: That’s right. Because you see he came down to New Orleans to do a piece that Alvin Batiste had written for soprano, soprano and alto. And the soprano part was out so he said, “Kidd, you done studied, you know all this” you know how he was. On like the alto they’d be playing all them top register things, he’d go to California and he heard Ernie Watts and them were doing all this, and say, “you know how to do this,” you know like all up the horn and the soprano, he hadn’t been playing the soprano, but they gave it to him. So I was dealing with the soprano, you know for him to get that stuff ‘cause it was written out. And it was a difficult part. And I told him I said, “look, don’t worry about it. If you don’t get it I got your back, I’ll go on and do it with the thing.” Shit man we set up that night with Cannon that next morning, he got drunk after it. He drank a pint of whiskey. The next morning he woke up and he had to come with some Maalox to get him up. But Jack, that night, he tore through that on that soprano like Grant went through Richmond. And he told me, “yeah, Kidd, next time watch, I’m gonna do some of the crazy stuff that you’re doing,” because I had some stuff on tape. And he listened to it. That’s the last thing he told me in his lifetime. “I’m gonna do some of that crazy stuff
you’re doing.” You just wait, I’m gonna get ya. Now if he had done some of that, and the way he is, oh man, Lord have mercy.
